title: Bark nitrophyte lichens increased in British records in 1986-2025, but not more at high NHx deposition in 10-km squares; SO2-tolerant acidophytes decreased most where SOx decreased most
abstract: We tested two explanations for the shift from acid-bark lichens (acidophytes) to nitrogen-loving lichens (nitrophytes) in Great Britain: high ammonia-type nitrogen (NHx) deposition, or the decrease of sulphur (SOx). We used 77,729 British Lichen Society recording visits from GBIF (1960-2025) and the van Herk indicator lists. Poisson models counted indicator species per visit, with list length as the effort control, and compared changes from 1986-1995 across 2,582 10-km squares with CBED deposition. Bark nitrophytes increased to about 1.5 times the 1987-1989 level in England and in Scotland and Wales. SO2-tolerant acidophytes decreased to 0.30 and 0.45. The nitrophyte gain did not follow NHx: +0.035 log units per SD (95% CI -0.029 to 0.099) in 2005-2012, against a national gain of about 0.29. Acidophytes decreased less, not more, at high NHx. SO2-tolerant acidophytes decreased most where SOx decreased most (-0.158 per SD; repeated in both regions and in 2013-2025). SO2-sensitive acidophytes and nitrophytes had no clear SOx term; common non-indicator bark lichens had the largest SOx gain. The planned model gave a negative NHx term for nitrophytes, but this came from fewer churchyard surveys after 1995; models that compare visits of the same survey type remove it. Limitations: opportunistic records without substrate, 10-km exposure, correlated NHx, NOx and SOx, CBED ends in 2012, and indicator-only download after 1991 because of GBIF rate limits.

display.caption: Indicator species per visit relative to 1987-1989, with the same list length, 10-km square and dataset subset. Bands are 95% CI. Bark nitrophytes increased and SO2-tolerant acidophytes decreased in England and in Scotland and Wales.

Change from 1986-1995 to 2005-2012 per 1 SD of NHx (A) and of SOx decrease (B), by group and model. The planned model (grey) differs from models that compare visits of the same survey type, because churchyard surveys decreased.

NHx and SOx-decrease terms for single taxa (at least 500 visits). Most acidophytes have a positive NHx term; SO2-tolerant acidophytes have negative SOx terms; common bark lichens have the largest positive SOx terms.
